statement_record.book: Informally, a diagram is a quiver of morphisms in a category, and it COMMUTES when any two paths of composable arrows with a common source and a common target have the same composite; e.g. the commutative triangle asserts h = g f.
statement_record.intree: Commutativity is expressed throughout as ≈-equations between composites in the hom-setoids, and is packaged as a proposition for the two standard shapes: the commuting SQUARE is the square-type of the double category `Sq C` (`dsq h u v k := k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h`, an honestly proof-irrelevant proposition) and the commuting TRIANGLE is `cone_coherence : fmap[F] f ∘ vertex_map x ≈ vertex_map y`; `is_pullback_commutes : f ∘ p1 ≈ g ∘ p2` is the same square condition inside the pullback record.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: commutativity is only ever stated shape-by-shape, as a named ≈-equation between two specific composites. There is no general predicate quantifying over ALL pairs of paths in a quiver.

gap: No general, quiver-indexed 'this diagram commutes' predicate. statement_record.book: A monoid is an object M of Set with morphisms mu : M × M → M and eta : * → M (with * a singleton) such that the associativity square mu ∘ (M × mu) = mu ∘ (mu × M) and the two unit triangles mu ∘ (eta × M) = id = mu ∘ (M × eta) commute; the diagrammatic phrasing generalizes verbatim to other categories.
statement_record.intree: `Class Monoid (X : C)` with mu : X ⨂ X ~> X, eta : I ~> X and exactly the three laws (mu_assoc, mu_unit_left, mu_unit_right), stated over an arbitrary monoidal base; Structure/Monoid.v's `MonoidObject` is the same class under the names mappend/mempty, and its `Monoid := @MonoidObject C CC_Monoidal` fixes ⨂ to the categorical product and I to the terminal object — the Set case, with `Sets_Cartesian` (Instance/Sets/Cartesian.v:32) and `Sets_Terminal` (Instance/Sets.v:248) supplying that structure.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-stronger: the library states the definition over an arbitrary monoidal base (the generalization Riehl only announces here and carries out in Definition 1.6.3 / §E.2), with the cartesian/Set case recovered by instantiation. Presentation differs only in that the associator and unitors are written explicitly rather than suppressed as they are in Set.

Class Functor {C : Category} {D : Category} := { fobj : C → D; fmap {x y : C} (f : x ~> y) : fobj x ~> fobj y; fmap_respects : ...; fmap_id {x : C} : fmap (@id C x) ≈ id; fmap_comp {x y z : C} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g }.

Class ACone {J : Category} {C : Category} (c : obj[C]) (F : J ⟶ C) := { vertex_map (x : J) : c ~{C}~> F x; cone_coherence {x y : J} (f : x ~{J}~> y) : fmap[F] f ∘ vertex_map x ≈ vertex_map y }  — J is explicitly the diagram's index category, and functoriality of F is what forces the image's composition relations.

statement_record.book: A diagram in a category C is a functor F : J → C; its domain J is called the indexing category or the shape of the diagram. No size restriction is imposed on J, and functoriality forces every composition relation holding in J to hold in the image, which is what it means for the image quiver to be commutative.
statement_record.intree: The library has `Class Functor {C D : Category}` with the two functoriality laws (fmap_id, fmap_comp) and uses an arbitrary `F : J ⟶ C` directly as the diagram everywhere a shape is needed — `Class ACone {J C} (c) (F : J ⟶ C)`, `Class Limit \`(F : J ⟶ C)` — with J an unrestricted `Category` (universe-polymorphic, no smallness field).
statement_record.strength_comparison: same, modulo naming: the library never introduces the abbreviation `Diagram F` nor the words 'indexing category'/'shape' as identifiers, but Riehl's Definition 1.6.4 asserts nothing beyond 'a diagram is a functor', and the role of J as the shape is realized literally by the domain of F throughout Structure/Cone.v and Structure/Limit.v. Like the book, no size restriction is imposed.

evidence.intree_statement: Program Definition Compose {C D E : Category} (F : D ⟶ E) (G : C ⟶ D) : C ⟶ E := {| fobj := fun x => fobj (fobj x); fmap := fun _ _ f => fmap (fmap f) |}  — the obligation discharged by `intros; rewrite !fmap_comp; reflexivity`, i.e. exactly Riehl's proof that GF : J ⟶ D is again a diagram.

fmap_respects : ∀ x y, Proper (equiv ==> equiv) (@fmap x y);  fmap_comp {x y z : C} (f : y ~> z) (g : x ~> y) : fmap (f ∘ g) ≈ fmap f ∘ fmap g  — together these say a functor carries any ≈-equation between composites to an ≈-equation between the images, which is the equational content of 'functors preserve commutative diagrams'.

statement_record.book: Lemma 1.6.5: Functors preserve commutative diagrams. Proof: a diagram in C is a functor F : J → C; for any G : C → D the composite GF : J → D is the image diagram in D, which therefore satisfies all the composition relations holding in J.
statement_record.intree: `Compose (F : D ⟶ E) (G : C ⟶ D) : C ⟶ E` — the composite of two functors is a functor, its functoriality obligation proved by `rewrite !fmap_comp` — together with the `fmap_comp` / `fmap_respects` fields of `Class Functor` which push any equation between composites through fmap.
statement_record.strength_comparison: same: Riehl's proof IS the observation that GF is a functor, and that is exactly what `Compose` asserts. The library additionally proves `Compose_respects` (Theory/Functor.v:272, composition is Proper for ≈ of functors) and `fobj_Compose`, which the book does not state.

Program Definition Sq (C : Category) : DoubleCategory := {| dcat := C; dhor := fun a b => a ~{C}~> b; dsq := fun a b c d h u v k => k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h; ... |} — commutative squares in C, packaged as the squares of a double category.

statement_record.book: The category 2 × 2 has four objects and the displayed non-identity morphisms; its diagonal is simultaneously the composite of top-then-right and of left-then-bottom, so those composites are equal. A diagram indexed by 2 × 2, drawn without the diagonal, is precisely a commutative square.
statement_record.intree: Both factors of the shape exist (`_2`, the walking arrow, and `Product`/`∏` on categories), and the notion of a commutative square in C exists independently as `dsq h u v k := k ∘ u ≈ v ∘ h` (Construction/Sq.v) and as `is_pullback_commutes : f ∘ p1 ≈ g ∘ p2` (Theory/Morphisms/Stability.v:55).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the shape and the notion it is supposed to index are both present, but the identification the example makes between them is not.

statement_record.book: In practice an indexing category is specified as a quiver together with imposed commutativity relations, and in the image the composite arrows are omitted. To give a functor out of 2 × 2 it suffices to name four objects and four morphisms f, g, h, k subject to h f = k g. The relations are essential data: they distinguish 2 × 2 (which indexes a commutative square) from the quiver-generated category with two distinct diagonals (which indexes a not-necessarily-commutative square).
statement_record.intree: Both halves of 'quiver + relations' are in-tree with their universal properties: `FreeOnQuiver G` (paths as morphisms) with `InducedFunctor`/`UniversalArrowQuiverCat`/`FreeForgetfulAdjunction` for the generators, and `Quotient C R` for a `HomCongruence R` with `QuotientLift` and `QuotientLift_unique` for the relations. The 'two distinct diagonals' phenomenon is even witnessed concretely elsewhere: `funny_diagonals_distinct` (Construction/Funny/Comparison.v:144) proves the two diagonals of the square in `_2 □ _2` are NOT identified.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the two universal properties exist separately and are never composed into a single presentation theorem, and the specific 2 × 2 instance is not carried out.

gap: Three things are missing. (1) No combined statement 'a functor out of FreeOnQuiver(G)/R is exactly a quiver homomorphism whose image satisfies R': the free-category UMP (Construction/Free/Quiver.v) and the quotient UMP (Construction/Quotient.v) are never chained, and no presentation-by-generators-and-relations construction for general categories exists (the only presentation machinery in-tree, Construction/PROP/Presentation.v and Construction/ColouredPROP/Presentation.v, is specific to PROPs and coloured PROPs). (2) The specific instance — the square quiver with the relation h f = k g yielding 2 × 2, and 'to define a functor out of 2 × 2 name four objects and four morphisms with h f = k g' — is not formalized (`_2 ∏ _2` never appears; see riehl:1.6:example6). (3) The contrast the remark turns on, between the free category on the square quiver (two distinct diagonals) and its quotient by h f = k g, is not stated for categories; the closest in-tree analogue is `funny_diagonals_distinct` for the funny tensor `_2 □ _2`, which is about the interchange law, not about a quiver presentation.
